_source: Drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from each course's catalog description, following the fingerprint guidelines in app/drafts.py. Shown as AI drafts until a person edits them.
6.4110: How can a POMDP be used to make decisions when the agent cannot observe the full state?
When would you choose Monte Carlo tree search over solving an MDP exactly, and what do you give up?
How does constraint propagation shrink a search space before you start backtracking?
How would you compute the probability of a hidden cause from evidence in a Bayesian network?
6.100A: How would you break a messy real-world problem into functions you can write and test one at a time?
Why does the choice between a list and a dictionary change how fast your program runs?
How do you find the bug when your program runs but gives the wrong answer?
When does defining your own class make a program easier to reason about?
6.1200: How would you prove that a property holds for every step of a program using an invariant?
When is strong induction the right tool, and what goes wrong if you use ordinary induction instead?
How do you count the ways to arrange objects when some of them are identical?
Why does RSA encryption work, and what would break it?
6.3900: Why can a model that fits its training data perfectly do worse on new data, and how do you detect it?
How does gradient descent find model parameters, and why can it get stuck?
What can a neural network represent that a linear classifier cannot?
How would you frame a real-world problem as a reinforcement learning task?
18.06: What does it mean geometrically when a system of equations has no solution, and what does least squares give you instead?
Why do eigenvalues tell you whether a repeated process grows, decays, or settles down?
How does the singular value decomposition let you compress an image or a dataset?
What do the four fundamental subspaces of a matrix tell you about the equations it represents?
14.01: Why might a price ceiling on rent reduce the number of apartments available?
How does a firm decide how much to produce when it can't set the market price?
Why does a monopoly produce less than a competitive market, and who loses?
When do markets fail to reach an efficient outcome, and what can policy do about it?
6.1010: How do you design a recursive solution, and how do you know it will terminate?
How would you structure a larger program so that each part can be tested on its own?
When is it worth replacing a slow, simple solution with a cleverer algorithm?
6.1210: How would you prove an algorithm is correct, not just that it works on your test cases?
When does a hash table beat a balanced search tree, and when does it lose?
How can you recognize a problem as a shortest-path or graph-search problem in disguise?
Why does dynamic programming turn some exponential-time problems into polynomial-time ones?
18.03: How do you model a physical system with a differential equation and predict its long-term behavior?
Why does a system resonate when it is driven at its natural frequency?
How do eigenvalues of a linear system tell you whether its solutions oscillate, grow, or decay?
How can you sketch the behavior of a nonlinear system without solving it exactly?
8.01: How do you decide which forces act on an object and predict its motion from them?
When is conservation of energy or momentum a faster route to an answer than Newton's laws?
Why does a spinning object resist changes to its axis of rotation?
18.01: What does a derivative tell you about how a quantity changes, and how do you use it to find an optimum?
Why does the fundamental theorem of calculus connect areas to rates of change?
How do you decide whether an infinite series adds up to a finite number?
18.02: How does the gradient tell you which direction a function increases fastest?
How do you set up and evaluate an integral over a region in two or three dimensions?
What do Green's, Stokes', and the divergence theorems say about flow through a boundary?
6.1910: How does a collection of logic gates become a processor that executes instructions?
Why does pipelining speed up a processor, and what hazards does it introduce?
Why does a memory hierarchy make most memory accesses fast even though main memory is slow?
24.900: How do linguists figure out the hidden rules that let speakers produce sentences they've never heard?
Why can no language or dialect be called simpler or better than another?
How do children acquire a language without being taught its grammar?
14.02: How do interest rate decisions by a central bank affect unemployment and inflation?
What determines a country's long-run economic growth?
What can fiscal policy do in a recession, and what are its costs?
